title: East-West Schism: the mutual excommunications of 1054
summary: On 16 July 1054 Cardinal Humbert, legate of Pope Leo IX, placed a bull excommunicating Patriarch Michael Cerularius on the altar of Hagia Sophia in Constantinople; Cerularius's synod then excommunicated the legates. Later tradition took this as the start of the Catholic-Orthodox split, but scholars now reject that view: talks continued, and the sack of 1204 is among later events that deepened the break.

uncertainty.note: Christian History Institute gives 16 July 1054; EBSCO gives 1054 only.

where.historical_name: Cathedral of Hagia Sophia, Constantinople, Byzantine Empire

importance.justification: Later tradition treated the episode as the beginning of the split between the Eastern (Orthodox) and Western (Catholic) churches.

sources.title: Wikidata item Q12506 (Hagia Sophia), coordinate location (P625)

reviewer_note: Whether 1054 was "the" schism is contested: EBSCO says it is unclear whether a state of schism existed, and Christian History Institute says scholars reject 1054 as the start. The day-level date rests on one source; EBSCO gives only 1054. The Wikidata pin is the present building.
